title.value: Why Should I Trust You, Bellman? The Bellman Error is a Poor Replacement for Value Error
title.justification: The title explicitly appears at the beginning of the research paper document.
title.quote: Why Should I Trust You, Bellman? The Bellman Error is a Poor Replacement for Value Error

analysis.description: This research paper investigates the relationship between the Bellman error and value prediction accuracy in reinforcement learning. It argues that the Bellman error is an inadequate proxy for the accuracy of value functions and demonstrates this through theoretical analysis, toy examples, and empirical studies. The work primarily focuses on policy evaluation, highlighting the shortcomings of using Bellman error in both on-policy and off-policy settings.

type.justification: The paper primarily provides theoretical analysis, propositions, and proofs regarding the inadequacy of the Bellman error as an objective for value function accuracy.
type.quote: We demonstrate these problems theoretically, with toy problems, and empirically on standard benchmark environments.

name.justification: The paper is centered around concepts such as the Bellman equation, policy evaluation, and value functions, which are fundamental components of reinforcement learning.
name.quote: In reinforcement learning (RL), value functions are a measure of performance of a target policy.

name.justification: The paper explicitly mentions that its focus is on policy evaluation, detailing the process and challenges associated with it.
name.quote: This work aims to better understand the relationship between the Bellman error and the accuracy of value functions through theoretical analysis and empirical study. We do so by focusing on the setting of policy evaluation.

name.justification: The paper discusses BRM as one of the models explored in relation to minimizing Bellman error.
name.quote: We focus largely on two algorithms based on the Bellman equation, which update an approximate value function Q, using samples from a finite dataset D. Bellman residual minimization (BRM) (Baird, 1995) directly minimizes the Bellman error over samples in the dataset D.

is_contributed.justification: BRM is referenced from prior work and is not a contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: Bellman residual minimization (BRM) (Baird, 1995) directly minimizes the Bellman error over samples in the dataset D.

is_executed.justification: BRM is included in the experimental evaluation, where its performance is analyzed.
is_executed.quote: We now examine if these problems occur in practice. Recall our main observations are (1) the magnitude of the Bellman error is smaller for biased value functions ... We find that both of these concerns exist clearly in standard benchmark environments.

is_compared.justification: BRM's performance is compared to other methods like FQE in terms of Bellman error and value error.
is_compared.quote: The lack of correlation between Bellman error and value error is highlighted by an empirical comparison between Bellman Residual Minimization (BRM) (Baird, 1995) and Fitted Q-Evaluation (FQE) (Ernst et al., 2005; Le et al., 2019), which shows that value functions trained with BRM consistently have much lower Bellman error, but much higher value error than value functions trained with FQE.
